headline: 34 trades net -1.06 bps/bet (-35.9 total); recent 6-bet window -16 bps net but tiny — soft, within noise, no signal active.
alert_message: Rolling window turned negative and cumulative net sits below breakeven, but sample is too thin to call a true breakdown. Keep running, keep watching.
regime_note: BTC ~$74.8k, still chopping through the mid-$70s with sharp two-sided 5-min swings — the volatile tape this fade is built for, so soft numbers can't be excused as a 'wrong regime.' No signal active right now.
assessment_md:
**How it's doing:** Marginal, as designed — and currently on the wrong side of breakeven. Across all 34 resolved trades the strategy averages **-1.06 bps/bet** (total **-35.9 bps**), with a low **38% win rate** that's partly offset by a few large winners (e.g. +49, +26 bps). Backing out the 3 bps cost, gross edge is running ~**1.9 bps/bet** — below the ~4 bps we expected and well under the ~3.9 bps it needs just to break even.

**What changed:** The short rolling window flipped from +1.3 bps net last time to **-16 bps net over 6 bets** (gross -13 bps despite a 67% win rate — meaning one or two outsized losers dominated). That's a deterioration in tone, but it's six trades.

**What the numbers do and don't tell us:** With 34 trades and ~20 bps of per-bet noise, the standard error on the mean is roughly 3+ bps — so a -1 bps average is **statistically indistinguishable from zero**. We cannot yet say the edge is broken; we also can't say it's working. Separately, the broader edge search still has **0 survivors** at a 5 bps cost bar — a reminder this family of signals is fragile.

**Bottom line:** No profit here, no clear catastrophe either. Results are consistent with a marginal, probably-not-net-profitable strategy. Keep collecting data; another couple dozen trades this soft would justify escalating.
